paper.title_en: Special unitary algebras underlying bipartite qubit and qutrit systems
paper.abstract_en: According to Ref. [11 ], in bipartite qubit systems, a matrix A exists such that $\text {Det}\, A = 0$ indicates unentanglement, whereas $\text {Det}\, A \ne 0$ indicates entanglement, and there exists an underlying SU(2) algebra. Here, we show that this algebra does not imply any internal degrees of freedom. Physical interpretation of the underlying algebras is given for the SU(2) case in the context of two entangled electrons. We also show that under a certain redefinition of matrices, the Clifford algebra satisfied by the usual 4-dimensional Dirac matrices is obtained. This redefinition is related to time reversal. In Ref. [11 ] it was shown that for qutrits there is a matrix P for which $\textrm{Det}\, P =0 $ simultaneously with $\textrm{Tr}\, P = \pm 1$ implies unentanglement. Any departure from these conditions implies entanglement, and there exists an underlying ${ SU}(3)$ algebra. The new results in this work are analytical solutions for the eigenvalues of the reduced density matrix corresponding to arbitrary bipartite qutrit states. The ${ SU}(3)$ algebra is obtained after a redefinition of variables. Here, we also obtain the entanglement entropy for both qubits and qutrits. For qubits, the entropy is in terms of $\textrm{Det}\,A$. For qutrits the entropy is expressed in terms of $\textrm{Det}\,P$ and $\textrm{Tr}\,P$.
